entries.summary: Use opt-in compositor manifests for bounded read-only binding and focus queries.
Capture terminal input when a controlling terminal is available.
Capture through the native compositor backend when Hyprland socket2 IPC is available.
Observe Sway binding events through IPC in pass-through mode; suppression is not exposed by Sway IPC.
Open a focused Wayland or X11 probe window and report whether the desktop delivered the key to a client or consumed it; the default listen chain uses it when native compositor capture is unavailable.
Emit one compact schema-v2 record per captured event.
Write replayable JSON or NDJSON capture records to an explicit file.
Capture Linux evdev keyboard events when a readable device is available.

Detect common pre-compositor remappers; evaluate the queried key against keyd, kanata, kmonad, input-remapper, and xremap configurations so remaps redirect and layer or command actions consume, keeping timing-dependent actions and kmonad or input-remapper rules for unproven devices conditional.
Detect IBus/Fcitx5 session context.
Query an active IBus/Fcitx5 engine through a read-only API when possible.
Use bounded read-only Fcitx5 D-Bus calls without launching client helpers.
Inspect Hyprland bindings, submaps, devices, and instance-scoped IPC.

Inspect Cinnamon global keybinding schemas.
Inspect MATE Marco and SettingsDaemon keybinding schemas.

Inspect literal River init mappings.
Inspect literal Wayfire binding settings.

Expose typed committed-text, Compose/dead-key, and application-preedit observability limits; passive capture does not reconstruct text history.
